text.p: Shares of Slovenian brokerage Dadas jumped 7.14 percent in early Thursday trade in what traders described as a technical reaction to Wednesday's 9.68 percent fall.
At 1000 GMT, Dadas was up 7.14 percent or 500 tolars at 7,500 tolars on volume of 50 shares.
"Such an increase does not mean much on low volumes like this," said Matjaz Lorencic, a trader at Mariborska BPH.
Traders said there was significant room for further long-term gains because of the company's bold business plans, but they cautioned the shares could be a risky investment in the short term.

"Dadas is offering franchises of many big companies, such as McDonalds, from various business fields. I doubt that will have a major impact on Dadas's price at the moment, but maybe sometime in the future," Lorencic added.

Trading volumes in Dadas have been poor since March last year when the Securities Market Agency started procedures to ban Dadas' brokerage arm from trading, claiming it was rigging prices among its affiliated companies.

Since then the share has fallen over 95 percent, while average daily volume dropped to about 50 shares a day from over 1,000 shares per day previously. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
